extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark tailored for long context understanding. It comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories (single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion) in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese). LongBench contains 4,750 test instances standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation of LLMs on long context tasks.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li (Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench is composed of 21 datasets organized into 6 major task categories. Among these datasets, 6 are directly extracted from original datasets provided by previous studies, 10 are built based on original datasets and processed to be suitable for long context evaluation, and 5 are created and annotated by the authors. Data extraction uses two strategies: random sampling (for LongBench) to maintain natural length distribution, and uniform sampling based on length (for LongBench-E) across ranges 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+ words.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources include: Literature/Film (NarrativeQA), Science papers (Qasper), Multi-field documents including legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers from Arxiv, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, Chinese Government Website (MultiFieldQA), Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en), Baidu Search (DuReader), Government reports (GovReport), Meetings (QMSum, VCSUM), News (MultiNews, LSHT), Web questions (TREC), Dialogues (SAMSum), C4 Dataset (PassageRetrieval-zh), Github repositories (LCC, RepoBench-P).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Multi-Doc QA, complete Wikipedia passages encompassing supporting or distracting paragraphs are used as context; supporting passages are included first, then distracting passages are added until reaching maximum length, and passages are randomly ordered. For DuReader, 20 documents including distractors are associated with each question. For Few-shot Learning tasks, a random integer within a range is chosen as the number of examples to sample from the training set and concatenate as context. For Synthetic tasks, PassageRetrieval uses GPT-3.5-Turbo to summarize randomly sampled passages. PassageCount randomly selects and repeats passages then shuffles them. For code completion, cross-file code snippets are shuffled and combined with in-file preceding code.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 21 datasets are standardized into a unified format (I, C, A) where I is input, C is long context, and A is answer. For TriviaQA, passages with less than 1,000 words are filtered. To avoid test leakage, data is extracted from test sets of public datasets (except VCSUM due to insufficient test data). When input length exceeds a model's maximum context length, the input sequence is truncated from the middle preserving the front and end.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA datasets (English and Chinese), three Ph.D. students manually annotated question-answer pairs for each article. Annotators were instructed to propose clear questions with definitive and relatively short answers, to ensure random distribution of evidence paragraphs throughout the article (avoiding positional bias), and to include varied question types (information-extracting, summarizing, multi-hop reasoning). Average annotation time was around 5 minutes per sample.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of NLP, positioning them as expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo was used to generate summaries for the PassageRetrieval synthetic tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors explicitly took measures during annotation of MultiFieldQA to avoid positional bias (ensuring evidence placement is random rather than at beginning or end of documents). The memorization analysis reveals that some datasets derived from Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue) may be subject to training data leakage, potentially inflating performance scores due to memorization rather than long context understanding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: (1) Potentially unreliable automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) which may not accurately reflect response quality and may underestimate results for models that generate longer responses. (2) Coupling with instruction-following capabilities—performance on LongBench is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities since tasks are close to real-world applications. Additionally, models may rely on memorization rather than context understanding for datasets derived from common pre-training sources like Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: LongBench is designed for Testing/Evaluation of LLMs' long context understanding abilities across 6 major task categories: single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. LongBench-E, a subset with evenly distributed context lengths, is designed specifically for gauging model capability across varying context lengths (0-4k, 4k-8k, 8k+).
